text: In nineteen ninety-five, a man walks into a Pittsburgh bank. No mask. Just a gun.
He even smiles at the security camera.
Then he robs a second bank, the very same afternoon.
His name is McArthur Wheeler. And he has a secret weapon.
A friend told him it works as invisible ink. So if you rub it on your face, cameras can't see you.
He even tests it. He covers his face in juice, and takes a Polaroid.
The photo comes out blank. He probably just missed.
The juice burns his eyes. He can barely see. But the plan feels perfect.
Three months later, police put the bank footage on the evening news.
And there he is. Crystal clear.
Within an hour, he is under arrest. And he cannot believe it.
But I wore the lemon juice!
The story reaches two psychologists, Dunning and Kruger.
They wonder. Can someone be too clueless to know they are clueless?
Their study becomes famous, as the Dunning-Kruger effect.
All thanks to one man, and a lemon.
